extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, and their attorneys/agents; USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance from the MPEP on (1) formal and substantive requirements for affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 and (2) invoking the prior-art exception for commonly owned or joint research agreement subject matter under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening disclosure exception when it is a generalization of inventor's prior disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If an intervening disclosure is simply a more general description of the subject matter previously publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor, the exception in 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B) or 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(B) applies to such subject matter of the intervening disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: inventor publicly disclosed a species and an intervening disclosure discloses a genus (a more generic disclosure of the species) — the intervening disclosure of the genus is not available as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) or (a)(2). Conversely, if the intervening disclosure is more specific than the inventor's prior disclosure (e.g., inventor disclosed a genus and intervening disclosure discloses a species), the intervening disclosure may be available as prior art unless the original disclosure would have caused PHOSITA to at once envision every species within that genus. Also applies to alternative species disclosed by intervening disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign and who may file an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.130
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone who has knowledge of the facts discussed in the declaration may sign a declaration under 37 CFR 1.130. However, it is the applicant or patent owner who may submit (file) an affidavit or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an assignee, obligated assignee, or person showing sufficient proprietary interest is the applicant under 35 U.S.C. 118, the applicant or their representative must file the affidavit/declaration even if the inventor or other knowledgeable party signed it. The affidavit/declaration must be filed by a party having authority to take action in the application. Authority to file generally does not lie with the inventor if the inventor is not the applicant (see MPEP § 2155.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for affidavits and declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit is a statement in writing made under oath before a notary public or other authorized officer; 37 CFR 1.68 permits a declaration to be used instead of an affidavit. The declaration must include an acknowledgment that willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declarant must state that all statements of the declarant's own knowledge are true and that statements made on information and belief are believed to be true. Exhibits filed with an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 must comply with 37 CFR 1.91 to be entered into the application file; exhibits that do not comply may be disposed of or returned to applicant. See MPEP § 602 et seq. for additional formal affidavit requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: When 37 CFR 1.130 is unavailable because of competing U.S. patent/application claiming same invention (derivation issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rejection is based upon a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication naming another inventor, and that patent/application claims the same or substantially the same invention as the applicant's, and the affidavit/declaration contends that an inventor named in the other application derived the claimed invention from the inventor/joint inventor in the applicant's application, the applicant or patent owner may need to file a petition for a derivation proceeding under 37 CFR 42.401 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting two different applicants to each aver that an inventor named in the other application derived the claimed invention without a derivation proceeding could result in issuance of two patents with patentably indistinct claims. Thus, 37 CFR 1.130 provisions are not available in certain situations to avoid issuance of two patents to different parties. 37 CFR 1.130 would be available, however, if (1) the rejection is based on a disclosure other than a U.S. patent/application publication; (2) the patent/application did not claim the same or substantially the same invention; or (3) the affidavit/declaration does not contend derivation by an inventor named in the other publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to decide sufficiency of affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: The question of sufficiency of affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 should be reviewed and decided by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of questions of formal sufficiency and propriety are by petition under 37 CFR 1.181 (answered by Technology Center Directors). Review on the merits of a 37 CFR 1.130 affidavit/declaration is by appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (see MPEP § 1201). Review of an examiner's refusal to enter an affidavit as untimely is by petition and not by PTAB appeal. Case law references: In re Deters; Ex parte Hale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely (seasonable) presentation of affidavits and declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 must be timely presented in order to be admitted. They are considered timely if submitted in one of the listed circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations are timely if submitted: (A) prior to a final rejection; (B) before appeal in an application not having a final rejection; (C) after final rejection but before or on the same date of filing an appeal, upon showing good and sufficient reasons why it was necessary and not earlier presented in compliance with 37 CFR 1.116(e); or (D) after prosecution is closed if filed with a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 in certain utility/plant applications (or CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) in design applications). All admitted affidavits/declarations are acknowledged and commented upon by the examiner in the next action and indicated on the Office Action Summary or cover sheet. For affidavits filed after appeal, see 37 CFR 41.33(d) and MPEP §§ 1206 and 1211.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art exception for commonly owned or joint research agreement subject matter (35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) provides that disclosures shall not be prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if the subject matter disclosed and the claimed invention, not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention, were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If properly invoked, the commonly owned or joint research agreement reference is not available as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) for both anticipation and obviousness rejections. See MPEP § 717.02(a) for invoking and § 717.02(b) for evaluating when the exception applies. This section applies to applications subject to AIA first-inventor-to-file; for non-AIA cases see other MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three statutory conditions under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) to invoke joint research agreement exception
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish that a joint research agreement makes the 102(b)(2)(C) exception applicable, three conditions must be satisfied: (1) subject matter disclosed must have been developed and claimed invention made by, or on behalf of, one or more parties to a joint research agreement that was in effect on or before the effective filing date; (2) the claimed invention must have been made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the joint research agreement; (3) the application must disclose, or be amended to disclose, the names of the parties to the joint research agreement (35 U.S.C. 102(c)(1)-(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'joint research agreement' is defined (35 U.S.C. 100(h)) as a written contract, grant, or cooperative agreement entered into by two or more persons or entities for performance of experimental, developmental, or research work in the field of the claimed invention. Joint research agreement subject matter under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) is treated under 37 CFR 1.104(c)(4)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'commonly owned' for 102(b)(2)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Commonly owned' means that the subject matter that would otherwise be prior art to the claimed invention and the claimed invention are entirely or wholly owned by, or under an obligation to assign to, the same person(s) or organization(s)/business entity(ies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common ownership requires 100% ownership of both the disclosed subject matter and the claimed invention; if less than 100% ownership exists, common ownership does not exist. Examples clarify that if multiple entities own the application, the disclosure relied upon must be owned by or under an obligation to assign to the same entities not later than the effective filing date. There is no requirement that the entire disclosure in the reference be commonly owned — only the subject matter relied upon for the rejection need be commonly owned (example: only first embodiment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and timing to establish common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: To invoke common ownership, the applicant or patent owner must provide a statement that the disclosure and the claimed invention were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention. A statement of present common ownership is not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should be on or begin on a separate sheet and must not be directed to other matters (37 CFR 1.4(c)); it must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33(b). The question of whether common ownership exists as of the effective filing date is determined on the facts of the case; moral or unenforceable obligations are insufficient. Because applicants/patent owners have the best knowledge and a duty of candor, their signed statement is sufficient unless the examiner has independent evidence raising material doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evidence that may be submitted to support common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant(s) or patent owner(s) may submit objective evidence in addition to the common ownership statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable evidence includes: (A) reference to assignments recorded in the USPTO under 37 CFR Part 3 that convey entire rights to the same person(s)/organization(s); (B) copies of unrecorded assignments conveying entire rights and filed in each application; (C) an affidavit/declaration by the common owner, filed in the application, stating common ownership and facts supporting it and properly signed by an empowered official; and (D) other evidence establishing common ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner response when independent evidence raises doubt about common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner has independent evidence that raises a material doubt as to the accuracy of the applicant's or patent owner's representation of common ownership, the examiner should explain the doubt and may require objective evidence of common ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: independent evidence may show lack of common ownership or obligation to assign. Examiners should note that execution dates in assignment documents may not reflect the date a party was under an obligation to assign, so further inquiry or evidence may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement and amendment requirements for invoking joint research agreement under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) and 37 CFR 1.71(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: To invoke the joint research agreement exception, the applicant or patent owner must provide a statement that the disclosure and claimed invention were made by or on behalf of parties to a joint research agreement, that the agreement was in effect on or before the effective filing date, and that the claimed invention resulted from activities within the agreement's scope. The statement must be on or begin on a separate sheet and signed per 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the names of the parties to the joint research agreement are not already in the application, the application must be amended to include the names in accordance with 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1). An amendment under 1.71(g)(1) may require the processing fee per 37 CFR 1.17(i) if not filed within specified timing windows (e.g., within three months of filing date, before first Office action on merits, etc.). If an amendment under 1.71(g) is filed after issue fee payment, the issued patent may not include names unless corrected by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323. Such amendments remain subject to rules of practice (e.g., 37 CFR 1.116, 1.121, 1.312).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of invoking common ownership or joint research agreement exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Once common ownership or a qualifying joint research agreement is properly established, the subject matter disclosed in the reference may not be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 35 U.S.C. 103 against the claims of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the reference could still be used as the basis for a double patenting rejection, if appropriate. Also, only the portion of the reference that is commonly owned or within the scope of the joint research agreement is excepted; other portions remain available as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability limited to AIA first-inventor-to-file contexts (editor notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP sections quoted (e.g., 717.01 and 717.02) are only applicable to applications subject to the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA (see 35 U.S.C. 100 (note) and MPEP § 2159).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103, see corresponding pre-AIA MPEP sections (e.g., MPEP §§ 716.10, 2146–2146.03) for analogous rules (including CREATE Act differences).
